workflow-0001.summary: Inherited thread-local state reused after process duplication and identifier collision
workflow: A multithreaded process stores per-thread execution state in thread-local storage.
The process is duplicated while other threads exist, leaving inherited state for threads absent in the child.
The child creates a worker whose thread identifier collides with a vanished parent thread.
Thread-local initialization retains the inherited entry instead of replacing it with the worker's state.
A later state lookup returns the stale entry, validation detects the mismatch, and the child terminates.

workflow-0002.summary: Unescaped substitution marker breaks display rendering
workflow: A user-supplied display string is accepted by an interface that supports template substitution.
The string contains a literal character reserved for substitution syntax without escaping it.
When the interface renders the display text, it interprets the character as a substitution directive and rejects the invalid directive instead of displaying the text.

workflow-0005.summary: Zero-length memory transfer with a null pointer
workflow: A container or buffer is empty, so its data pointer may be null.
An operation computes a transfer length of zero.
The implementation still invokes a low-level memory-transfer operation with the null pointer.
Pointer preconditions are violated despite the zero length, producing undefined-behavior diagnostics and potentially unsafe optimization assumptions.

workflow-0008.summary: Concurrent iterator exhaustion releases shared sequence during another retrieval
workflow: Multiple worker threads consume a shared iterator without synchronized cursor and lifetime coordination.
One thread reaches exhaustion and releases the iterator’s reference to the underlying sequence while another thread has already observed that sequence as available.
The second thread continues reading the sequence, while unsynchronized cursor updates can also race between workers.
The released sequence may be reclaimed or its ownership state corrupted, causing invalid memory access or process termination instead of clean exhaustion.

workflow-0009.summary: Post-overflow validation of signed output-size arithmetic is defeated by optimization
workflow: A text-building operation computes an output size by multiplying or adding signed integer quantities.
A large valid input makes the intermediate arithmetic exceed the signed integer range before validation.
The implementation checks for overflow afterward using the wrapped result, such as reversing the arithmetic or comparing it with the prior size.
Undefined signed overflow lets an optimizing compiler remove or invalidate the check.
The corrupted size reaches allocation or copying logic, causing a crash instead of a size-limit error.

workflow-0010.summary: Out-of-range floating-point narrowing occurs before representability validation
workflow: A caller supplies a floating-point value for conversion into a narrower numeric representation.
Rounding, scaling, or splitting produces a result outside the destination type’s representable range.
The implementation performs the narrowing conversion before checking whether the result fits.
The out-of-range conversion has undefined behavior, so later validation cannot reliably report an overflow error.ﬁ

workflow-0011.summary: Intermittent invalid memory access during heterogeneous numeric comparison
workflow: A comparison workload repeatedly compares values drawn from several numeric representations.
On some 32-bit environments, one mixed comparison intermittently reaches an invalid memory location.
The invalid access terminates the process, while repeating the same workload may succeed.

workflow-0013.summary: Empty instruction sequence causes boundary-overrun during execution
workflow: An executable object accepts an empty instruction sequence without enforcing a minimum instruction size.
Execution begins and assumes the sequence contains a fixed-width instruction.
Instruction decoding reads past the end of the empty backing buffer because no effective boundary check is performed.
The out-of-bounds read terminates the process instead of rejecting the malformed executable object.

workflow-0014.summary: Borrowed or derived handles are used after reentrancy, concurrency, mutation, or teardown invalidates their owner or backing storage.
workflow: A buffer-owning object allocates storage containing data, and another handle retains a pointer or reference into that storage.
The owner is released or destroyed, deallocating the storage while the derived pointer remains reachable.
A later read uses the retained pointer as though its backing storage were still valid.
The dereference accesses freed memory, triggering a use-after-free failure or unsafe behavior.

workflow-0017.summary: Heterogeneous sequence element misinterpreted as a different record type
workflow: A parser refactor changes recursive argument collection to an iterative sequence-building helper.
The helper receives a heterogeneous sequence containing wrapper records and assumes its elements are expression records.
It interprets the final wrapper as an expression and reads fields at offsets that do not belong to that object.
The invalid field access becomes a heap buffer overflow, causing sanitizer-detected process termination instead of successful parsing.

workflow-0021.summary: Instrumented allocation failure aborts instead of returning a recoverable error
workflow: A stress test intentionally drives a computation to request an extremely large memory allocation to verify graceful allocation failure.
A runtime configured with memory-error instrumentation treats the impossible allocation as fatal and terminates the process instead of returning an allocation-failure result.
The test expects the operation to continue and report a recoverable memory error.
The process exits before the expected error can be checked, causing the test suite to fail.

workflow-0022.summary: Forked child deadlocks on an inherited runtime mutex during worker creation
workflow: A multithreaded process is duplicated while another thread holds an internal mutex in a runtime instrumentation layer.
The child inherits the locked mutex, but the thread that could release it does not exist in the child.
The child starts a worker, and thread initialization tries to acquire the inherited mutex while preparing worker metadata.
The mutex acquisition cannot complete, so worker creation blocks indefinitely and the dependent operation hangs.

workflow-0024.summary: Error recovery dereferences missing diagnostic source data
workflow: A parser receives malformed text combining a continuation marker, line breaks, and an unclosed delimiter.
Initial tokenization records a lexical error while parsing also fails.
Error recovery resets state and performs a second parsing pass that replaces the earlier lexical error with a structural delimiter error.
The structural error reporter assumes source-line data is available, but recovery has left that data absent.
Diagnostic construction dereferences the missing data and terminates the process instead of returning a recoverable syntax error.

workflow-0025.summary: Cross-module inherited annotations resolved in the wrong namespace
workflow: A class-generation mechanism inherits fields whose type annotations remain deferred textual references from their defining module.
A derived class in another module generates a new initializer but associates those references with the derived class’s namespace.
A later annotation-resolution operation evaluates the references where the original types are absent or shadowed.
Annotation resolution fails or produces incorrect results instead of reconstructing the inherited types.

workflow-0026.summary: Link-time optimization produces an out-of-range branch
workflow: A large software build enables whole-program link-time optimization on a target architecture with limited branch reach.
The optimization and code-generation pipeline combines code into a layout where a branch target falls outside the instruction encoding's permitted range.
The assembler or linker rejects the generated machine code instead of producing the executable.
The build aborts during an intermediate executable's creation, while disabling link-time optimization allows the build to complete.

workflow-0028.summary: Forked child leaks inherited resources from vanished threads
workflow: A multithreaded process is duplicated while other worker threads still own runtime allocations and stacks.
The child retains those resources even though the corresponding worker threads do not continue running there.
Child shutdown does not reclaim all inherited resources.
Leak detection reports the residual allocations, causing the child to exit unsuccessfully instead of completing normally.

workflow-0029.summary: Nonportable configuration generation emits an invalid script
workflow: A build-configuration generator relies on an external text-processing tool to produce a shell script containing generated configuration data.
The required tool is unavailable or incompatible in the build environment, so a multi-line editing fragment is emitted without being applied correctly.
The configuration process executes that fragment as shell syntax instead of transforming it into valid script content.
Script parsing fails, aborting configuration instead of reporting the missing or incompatible tool clearly.

workflow-0030.summary: Signed bit-packing shift overflows before safe encoding
workflow: A low-level runtime builds a packed bit representation by left-shifting a value stored in a signed integer.
A valid runtime value and shift distance produce a result outside the signed integer type's representable range.
The signed left shift invokes undefined behavior before any safe conversion or validation occurs.
Undefined-behavior instrumentation reports a runtime error during ordinary program startup, although execution may continue.

workflow-0033.summary: Null base pointer offset computed before validation
workflow: A valid call path supplies no argument array because there are no values to package.
The implementation computes an offset from the null base pointer before checking whether the resulting sequence is empty or the pointer is usable.
Null-pointer arithmetic violates language rules and is exposed by runtime diagnostics or compiler assumptions.
The operation terminates instead of safely handling the empty argument sequence.

workflow-0034.summary: Instrumented custom-allocator metadata access aborts initialization
workflow: A build enables memory-error instrumentation across a runtime that also uses a custom allocator for small objects.
An instrumented helper starts and initializes internal mapping state.
Initialization resizes a mapping and releases its previous storage.
The custom allocator classifies the released pointer using metadata that is incompatible with the instrumented allocation environment.
That classification reads outside valid heap storage, so instrumentation aborts the helper and the build reports a downstream command failure.

workflow-0036.summary: Unchecked truncated metadata decoding leaks adjacent memory
workflow: An object contains truncated variable-length metadata that appears to contain an encoded record.
A metadata iterator reads the expected fields without verifying that enough bytes remain in the metadata buffer.
A zero-length decoded range causes iteration to continue past the valid terminator and consume adjacent memory as if it were metadata.
The decoded bytes expose unrelated heap data instead of producing a recoverable malformed-input error.

workflow-0037.summary: Extended diagnostic text exceeds fixed display capacity
workflow: A diagnostic string has fixed-size storage and already contains variable-length version and toolchain metadata.
A change appends additional build-configuration details without accounting for the complete output length.
The combined text exceeds the available display capacity and is truncated.
Users receive incomplete or misleading diagnostic information instead of the full build description.

workflow-0040.summary: Insufficient lookahead causes out-of-bounds read during character-sequence encoding
workflow: A text encoder receives a valid character sequence whose representation may require examining a following character.
The encoder probes each candidate representation using a pointer to only the current character while a candidate path assumes a second character is available.
That path reads beyond the supplied input boundary while handling the multi-character representation.
The out-of-bounds read is detected by memory-safety instrumentation or causes a process-terminating failure instead of reporting an encoding result.

workflow-0042.summary: Uninitialized unused numeric storage is read before neutralizing arithmetic
workflow: A low-level numeric object is created with zero magnitude, leaving its first storage unit uninitialized because it is considered unused.
A value-conversion helper reads that storage unit without first checking whether the magnitude is zero.
The indeterminate value is used in arithmetic that is expected to neutralize it, such as multiplication by zero.
Memory-safety instrumentation reports the uninitialized read and terminates the operation instead of allowing the conversion to complete.

workflow-0044.summary: Expected runtime leak aborts sanitizer-instrumented build validation
workflow: A sanitizer-enabled build runs a subprocess to validate dynamically loaded components.
The subprocess initializes runtime objects and performs ordinary validation work.
Shutdown leaves an allocation reachable because multi-phase initialization and finalization do not fully reclaim runtime state.
Leak detection treats the residual allocation as fatal and returns failure instead of allowing the validation to complete.
The build reports a failed validation step even though the component checks themselves succeeded.

workflow-0045.summary: Stale per-code instrumentation metadata triggers a pre-refresh version assertion
workflow: A runtime-wide monitoring configuration changes, incrementing the active monitoring version while some immutable code objects retain instrumentation metadata from the previous、st覆盖
Execution later reaches an event in one of those stale code objects before its instrumentation metadata is refreshed for the current runtime version.
The event dispatcher asserts that the code object's version matches the runtime-wide version instead of first synchronizing or validating the object's monitoring state.
The failed consistency assertion aborts the process during otherwise ordinary monitored execution.

workflow-0046.summary: Stale lookup cache retains a released replaced value
workflow: A runtime caches a lookup result for a member of a type-like object.
The underlying member mapping is mutated through a path that bypasses cache invalidation, replacing the old value and releasing it.
A later lookup reuses the stale cache entry, whose pointer still refers to the released value.
The lookup reads metadata from the freed value, causing a use-after-free crash instead of returning the replacement.

workflow-0047.summary: Unrestored environment mutation causes test-suite failure
workflow: A test or support routine changes process-wide environment state.
The routine finishes without restoring the original environment.
The test harness compares environment state before and after execution.
The residual change is detected and the overall test run is marked failed.
A test launches a subprocess and waits for it to signal readiness within a fixed short timeout.
Execution instrumentation and parallel system load slow startup and readiness signaling beyond that deadline.
The wait expires before the subprocess becomes ready, producing a timeout or readiness error.
The test reports failure even though the subprocess may complete correctly given a longer environment-adjusted timeout.

workflow-0050.summary: Incompatible callback signature hidden by function-pointer cast
workflow: A runtime registers object callbacks whose parameter types are narrower than the generic callback interfaces require.
The callbacks are forced into those interfaces through incompatible function-pointer casts.
Normal dispatch invokes the callbacks through the generic signatures, despite their concrete definitions having different types.
Undefined behavior instrumentation detects the mismatched indirect call and terminates or reports the operation instead of completing normally.

workflow-0052.summary: Unchecked argument-conversion failure causes downstream crash
workflow: A reconfiguration operation receives an argument of an unsupported type or a value whose conversion raises an exception.
The implementation invokes a conversion helper that reports failure but does not immediately check its result.
It continues by using the missing intermediate value or performing another conversion while the earlier exception remains pending.
Downstream processing encounters the invalid state and crashes instead of propagating a recoverable argument error.

workflow-0056.summary: Tokenizer pointer-index overflow during continued multiline input
workflow: Interactive input combines an opening delimiter, a line-continuation marker, a newline, and a following expression.
The tokenizer carries the continued construct across the newline and computes a character position using an invalid or overflowing offset.
The resulting pointer-index arithmetic exceeds the representable address range, triggering undefined-behavior diagnostics during otherwise valid input processing.
The runtime reports the diagnostic but continues instead of crashing; the affected path is encountered only once per session.

workflow-0057.summary: Concurrent permanent-retention transition races with owner reference counting
workflow: Multiple threads access a shared pool of deduplicated values while independently updating ownership and reference-count state.
One thread attempts to permanently retain an existing value that is still owned by another thread.
The retention transition writes the value’s ownership and reference-count metadata non-atomically while the owning thread performs concurrent reference-count operations.
The race corrupts or inconsistently observes the metadata, causing a memory-safety failure or process termination instead of safely retaining the value.

workflow-0058.summary: Invalid diagnostic argument type causes out-of-bounds formatting read
workflow: A caller supplies a non-text value where a diagnostic path expects a text object.
Validation detects the invalid value and enters error-reporting logic.
The diagnostic formatter interprets the non-text object using the text-object layout instead of rejecting the type safely.
Formatting reads beyond the object's allocation, causing a heap-buffer-overflow and process termination instead of returning the intended type error.

workflow-0059.summary: Optimization-pass ordering leaves redundant control-flow edge
workflow: A control-flow optimizer processes constant-dependent conditional branches and redirected jumps in the same optimization phase.
It tries to redirect an incoming jump before the target block’s constant condition has been simplified into an unconditional jump.
The later simplification changes the target control flow, leaving the earlier jump redundant.
The cleanup phase does not fully converge before its invariant check, so the remaining redundant jump violates the optimizer’s internal consistency assertion and terminates the run

workflow-0061.summary: Profiling instrumentation breaks configuration probes and causes a misleading incomplete-type build failure
workflow: A build enables an optional profiling or instrumentation mode, adding its compiler and linker flag to generated commands.
On an affected toolchain and runtime combination, executables built with that flag fail immediately because a required process-environment symbol cannot be resolved.
Configuration probes run those executables, interpret the failures as negative capability results, and generate incorrect feature settings.
The main build then omits a conditional type definition while embedding that type by value in a larger record.
Compilation fails with an incomplete-type error instead of reporting the underlying toolchain or runtime incompatibility.

workflow-0064.summary: Cross-context shared state outlives its owner
workflow: An embeddable runtime initializes and loads a built-in extension that stores interpreter-owned objects in legacy process-global module state.
Initialization and shutdown are repeated, but the extension state is not associated with each interpreter’s lifecycle.
Shutdown cannot fully clear and reclaim references retained by the shared extension state.
Each initialization cycle leaves additional allocations or references reachable, so leak detection reports persistent memory growth after otherwise successful shutdown.

workflow-0067.summary: Garbage-collector traversal overruns special static records
workflow: A runtime stores special immutable records in a static array that does not provide the full storage expected for ordinary collectible objects.
The object type is marked as eligible for garbage-collection traversal without distinguishing those special records.
The collector invokes the type’s traversal logic on a special record and reads fields beyond that record’s valid bounds.
The out-of-bounds access is detected as a global memory-safety failure and terminates the process instead of skipping the noncollectible record.

workflow-0073.summary: Unchecked oversized geometry causes downstream arithmetic corruption and crash
workflow: A caller supplies an extremely large coordinate or dimension to an interface that accepts region geometry.
The interface forwards the value without checking it against the downstream component’s supported geometry range.
The downstream component uses the value in internal layout or address arithmetic, producing invalid state or a corrupted pointer.
Region construction dereferences the invalid address and terminates the process instead of returning a bounds error.

workflow-0074.summary: Instrumented fatal-error reporting deadlocks and hangs the process
workflow: A diagnostic test intentionally triggers a fatal runtime error in an instrumented multithreaded process.
The fatal-error path invokes crash-reporting logic while the instrumentation and runtime are in an incompatible locking or signal-handling state.
Crash reporting cannot complete under that combination, so the process hangs instead of terminating and returning the expected failure.

workflow-0075.summary: Reentrant asynchronous handler invocation exhausts recursion depth
workflow: A stress workload repeatedly changes a process-wide event handler while another execution context rapidly emits asynchronous notifications.
A notification arrives while the handler is still executing, and the runtime permits the same handler to be entered reentrantly.
Repeated nested notifications invoke the handler again before earlier invocations return.
Nesting grows until the runtime’s recursion limit is exceeded, producing a recursion failure instead of completing the handler-update workload.

workflow-0076.summary: Unsupported protocol-family result causes server binding failure
workflow: A build or environment disables an optional network protocol family.
A server setup performs endpoint discovery without restricting results to supported protocol families.
Discovery returns an endpoint using the disabled family.
The setup attempts to bind using that unsupported family and fails with a low-level family error instead of selecting a supported family.

workflow-0077.summary: Concurrent contexts access shared process-wide state without a complete synchronization or publication protocol
workflow: Multiple isolated execution contexts run concurrently and access shared process-wide metadata, configuration, or resources.
One context initializes, updates, or tears down shared state while another reads or uses it.
The shared accesses lack sufficient atomic coordination or locking, producing data races and, for resources such as descriptors, concurrent close/use.
Race-detection instrumentation reports the unsynchronized access, causing the affected concurrent tests to fail or be skipped instead of completing normally.

workflow-0079.summary: Incomplete nested configuration cleanup leaks allocated settings
workflow: A configuration object allocates heap-backed strings and lists for its nested settings.
Cleanup releases the outer configuration object but does not traverse and free those nested allocations.
Repeated configuration creation and cleanup leaves the nested storage reachable as leaks.
Leak detection reports persistent memory growth instead of clean reclamation.

workflow-0080.summary: Callback re-entrancy invalidates borrowed state or backing storage during a native operation
workflow: A container clears entries whose value storage is embedded in an owning object.
Releasing one value invokes user cleanup code that re-enters and mutates the same container.
The re-entrant mutation changes or releases the embedded storage while the original clearing operation still holds its address.
The clearing operation continues through the invalidated storage, causing a use-after-free and process-terminating memory failure.

workflow-0081.summary: Underestimated external capacity defeats a backpressure test expectation
workflow: A test estimates usable external buffer capacity from a reported size.
It assumes the report accurately bounds how much data the system can accept and writes only that amount.
The system accepts more data than reported, so the intended backpressure state is not reached.
The test asserts that backpressure must already be observable and fails even though the I/O operation remains valid.

workflow-0083.summary: Undersized alternate signal stack overruns heap storage
workflow: A fault-reporting subsystem allocates an alternate signal-handling stack using a fixed size heuristic.
The target environment requires more signal-handler stack space than the heuristic reserves.
A fault or diagnostic signal runs on the undersized alternate stack and writes beyond its heap buffer.
Later shutdown frees the corrupted buffer, and memory instrumentation detects the out-of-bounds access and terminates the process.

workflow-0084.summary: Dependency behavior change invalidates a narrow test expectation
workflow: A test assumes a size option accepts only integer values and expects the corresponding integer-validation error for invalid input.
An external UI toolkit changes that option to accept general screen-distance values, including unit-bearing strings.
The unchanged test submits invalid input and receives a distance-parsing error instead of the previously expected integer error.
The assertion compares against the obsolete diagnostic and reports a test failure despite the underlying operation behaving correctly.

workflow-0087.summary: Reachability-unaware code generation produces compiler diagnostics
workflow: A code generator emits generic cleanup, error-handling, and loop logic for low-level operation handlers without fully tracking reachability or compile-time-disabled branches.
Some generated handlers terminate with a return or jump, while other conditions are known to be impossible in a supported configuration.
The generator still emits statements after those termination points and retains branches or loops whose bodies cannot execute.
The compiler diagnoses the generated constructs as unreachable or unused code, producing build warnings or failures instead of clean generated output.

workflow-0088.summary: Instrumented subprocess failure is surfaced as a test assertion
workflow: A test suite runs multiple process- and thread-heavy tests in parallel under race-detection instrumentation.
A subprocess-based import operation executes within that stressed instrumented environment.
The subprocess exits with a non-success status instead of completing successfully.
The test harness treats the unexpected exit status as an assertion failure and reports the test failure.

workflow-0090.summary: Concurrent lazy-cache initialization races during shared value publication
workflow: Multiple threads request a cached value for the same shared object while the cache is marked absent.
Each thread independently computes the value and writes it to the shared cache without synchronization.
Concurrent reads and writes to the cache create a data race during publication of the lazily initialized value.
Instrumentation detects the race, causing the operation or test to fail instead of safely reusing the cached value.

workflow-0091.summary: Error-path ownership loss in native operations
workflow: A source-processing operation allocates an intermediate value while decoding input text.
Later validation rejects an invalid argument and raises a recoverable error.
The exceptional cleanup path fails to release the intermediate allocation.
Leak detection reports the unreclaimed allocation after the operation exits.

workflow-0094.summary: Stale system configuration header overrides current build header
workflow: A source-tree build generates a configuration header for the current build.
The compiler searches a system-wide configuration header from an older installation before finding the build-generated header.
Compilation combines stale configuration definitions with current source declarations, creating conflicting macros and types.
The compiler rejects the build instead of using the current configuration or reporting the header-selection problem clearly.

workflow-0096.summary: Independent feature and version checks redefine one compiler configuration symbol
workflow: A build supports two alternative spellings for a compiler annotation that disables a selected class of diagnostics.
Capability detection on a newer compiler recognizes the modern spelling and defines one shared configuration symbol for it.
A separate version-based compiler check independently defines the same configuration symbol using the legacy spelling.
The compiler reports a duplicate definition instead of completing the build; guarding the fallback definition against an existing symbol resolves the conflict.

workflow-0097.summary: Concurrent shutdown races with a still-running worker on shared state
workflow: Multiple worker threads perform operations using shared native library state.
Process termination begins and cleanup releases that shared state while workers are still active.
A worker continues through the operation after the cleanup has invalidated the state it relies on.
The worker accesses the released state and crashes instead of being synchronized with shutdown.

workflow-0100.summary: Concurrent access to mutable shared state without effective synchronization or lifetime protection
workflow: A shared resource object stores a mutable native handle used by concurrent operations.
One thread closes or detaches the resource and changes the handle while another thread is using it.
The reader and writer access the handle without synchronization or atomic coordination.
The concurrent accesses form a data race, producing sanitizer failure and potentially invalid resource use instead of safe operation handling.

workflow-0104.summary: Removing sanitizer suppression exposes deliberate fault-trigger and mismatched-dispatch undefined behavior
workflow: A low-level component uses deliberate undefined operations to trigger fault handling and dispatches specialized callbacks through generic interfaces with incompatible signatures.
Undefined-behavior sanitizer suppression hides these invalid operations and indirect calls, allowing the tests or build to appear successful.
The suppression is removed so instrumentation evaluates the fault-triggering and callback-dispatch paths directly.
The sanitizer reports a fatal undefined-behavior failure instead of allowing the intended fault signal or callback operation to complete.
The implementation must replace fabricated undefined behavior with explicit signaling and use signature-correct dispatch wrappers.

workflow-0105.summary: Concurrent unsynchronized access to shared collection-accounting state
workflow: Multiple worker threads use a shared iterator while other threads mutate its underlying collection and advance or exhaust the iterator.
Iterator position, exhaustion, and collection-size state are read and updated concurrently without sufficient synchronization or atomic coordination.
One operation observes iterator or collection state while another changes it, producing inconsistent shared state and a data race.
The race can yield invalid iteration behavior or sanitizer-detected process termination instead of stable length reporting and exhaustion handling.

workflow-0109.summary: Partial instrumentation causes a false-positive uninitialized read during startup
workflow: An application enables uninitialized-memory instrumentation but links against prebuilt dependencies that were not instrumented.
Startup initializes a valid string-like key through the uninstrumented code, leaving instrumentation metadata for part of its storage unavailable.
An instrumented lookup or hashing operation scans the key and treats the missing metadata as an uninitialized byte.
The instrumentation reports a fatal uninitialized read during normal startup even though the underlying value and memory access are valid.

workflow-0110.summary: Missing instrumentation guard exposes stack overflow in deep-recursion test
workflow: A test intentionally exercises recursion requiring an unusually deep call stack.
A compatibility guard skips the test for some instrumentation modes but does not recognize the active memory-safety instrumentation mode.
The recursive workload exhausts the available stack under that instrumentation.
The instrumented runtime aborts on stack overflow, so the test fails instead of being skipped.

workflow-0111.summary: Default configuration overrides an explicit allocator selection
workflow: A build configuration enables memory-error instrumentation and explicitly selects a custom memory allocator.
Configuration logic applies the instrumentation mode's default allocator setting without checking whether the user supplied an explicit allocator choice.
The default setting overrides the explicit selection, so the requested allocator is silently disabled.
The build proceeds with unintended allocator behavior instead of honoring the valid combined configuration.

workflow-0112.summary: Lock-held global pause creates circular wait
workflow: One worker acquires a shared coordination lock and then requests a global pause requiring other workers to reach a safe point.
Another worker attaches its execution state and tries to acquire the same lock before reaching that safe point.
The first worker waits for the global pause while the second waits for the lock.
Neither worker can proceed, so the operation deadlocks instead of completing.

workflow-0114.summary: Misaligned typed access during raw code-buffer patching
workflow: A code-generation component patches values into raw byte storage at locations that are not guaranteed to meet the values’ alignment requirements.
The implementation reinterprets those locations as pointers to wider typed values and performs direct reads or writes through them.
The misaligned typed access violates alignment and representation rules, so sanitizer instrumentation reports undefined behavior and the operation can terminate with a memory fault
A user supplies an unusually large valid input that exercises an optimized execution path.
The optimizer allocates a generated execution object while preparing that operation.
The generated object is not released after the optimized execution completes.
Leak detection reports the unreclaimed allocation instead of clean termination.

workflow-0120.summary: Unnecessary tracking of cycle-ineligible immutable containers degrades collection performance
workflow: A runtime begins registering every newly created immutable aggregate container with its cycle-detecting collector, regardless of whether its contents can participate in cycles.
An application creates many immutable containers holding only non-collectible values during ordinary execution.
Collection cycles repeatedly scan those containers even though they cannot contribute to reclaimable cycles.
The unnecessary tracking work causes a substantial garbage-collection performance regression instead of allowing such containers to remain untracked.

workflow-0125.summary: Feature-guard mismatch exposes unavailable interface member
workflow: A build condition enables an optional group of interface fields when a coarse feature marker is present.
The target’s system headers define that marker but lack one newer member of the associated data structure.
Generated binding code references the unavailable member without a narrower availability guard.
Compilation fails with a missing-member error instead of omitting the unsupported field or reporting the compatibility mismatch.

workflow-0126.summary: Concurrent table publication exposes partially initialized record
workflow: Multiple threads concurrently read and update a shared hash-indexed table without sufficient synchronization or publication ordering.
An updater marks a table slot as occupied before fully initializing the record referenced by that slot.
A lookup observes the occupied slot while the record contents are still absent or incomplete.
The lookup dereferences the incomplete record state, causing a crash instead of safely observing a consistent table entry.

workflow-0127.summary: Shutdown leaves a blocking background worker un-terminated
workflow: A standalone service starts a background worker that blocks waiting for incoming connections.
Shutdown signals the service’s main loop and request handlers but does not signal the connection-accepting worker.
The accepting worker remains blocked and continues running after shutdown begins.
Instrumentation checks teardown and reports the still-live worker as a thread leak, causing shutdown validation to fail.

workflow-0129.summary: Unsupported target accepted until generated-artifact build failure
workflow: A user enables an optional code-generation feature for a target environment that the feature does not support.
Configuration accepts the feature without validating that the target is among the generator's recognized targets.
The build invokes the generator with the unsupported target description, which rejects it and does not produce the generated header.
Compilation then fails because source files require the missing generated header instead of reporting the unsupported feature during configuration.

workflow-0132.summary: Null pointer passed to a native routine requiring valid string storage
workflow: A foreign-function call supplies a null pointer for an argument that requires valid character storage.
The native routine assumes the argument is non-null and attempts to determine the referenced string's length.
The length operation dereferences the null address.
The invalid memory access terminates the process instead of producing a recoverable argument error.

workflow-0135.summary: Garbage-collector traversal dereferences partially initialized object state
workflow: A newly created managed execution object is registered for collection before all fields needed by the collector’s traversal logic are initialized.
A later setup operation can trigger collection while the object remains partially initialized.
The collector traverses the object and reads an uninitialized field as though it contained valid state.
The invalid state is dereferenced during traversal, causing a segmentation fault instead of safe collection.],

workflow-0137.summary: Reentrant user-code execution invalidates native state before later use
workflow: An operation validates that its backing resource is attached and begins converting a caller-supplied position-like value.
The conversion invokes user-defined code that detaches or releases the backing resource, clearing the handle while the outer operation continues.
The outer operation fails to revalidate the resource after conversion returns.
It calls through the cleared handle, causing a null dereference and process termination instead of a recoverable detached-resource error.

workflow-0138.summary: Error path omits cleanup of partially acquired temporary values
workflow: A multi-input operation retrieves and owns temporary values from earlier inputs.
A strict consistency check detects exhaustion or another error before all inputs are processed.
The error path returns without releasing the values already acquired.
Repeated failing operations retain those temporary values, causing memory usage to grow and leak detection to report unreclaimed allocations.

workflow-0140.summary: Unchecked executable metadata type causes later invalid dereference
workflow: A caller replaces a compiled executable object's constant metadata with values of an incompatible type.
The replacement is accepted without validating that the metadata matches the executable representation's invariants.
Execution later treats the malformed entries as valid managed objects while constructing a runtime object.
The invalid representation is dereferenced, causing a segmentation fault instead of a recoverable metadata error.

workflow-0147.summary: Borrowed field retained without ownership increment becomes dangling
workflow: A reconstruction helper builds a composite result containing a field borrowed from a still-live source object.
The builder treats the borrowed field as an owned reference without incrementing its ownership count.
The source object is released, deallocating the field while the composite result still retains its pointer.
Later cleanup or access through the composite result uses the dangling pointer, causing a heap memory-safety failure.

workflow-0149.summary: Unchecked enumeration of retained inactive resource entries
workflow: A resource registry retains an entry after the associated resource is closed, destroyed, or released, clearing the entry’s backing-resource pointer.
An enumeration operation allocates output storage using the count of currently active resources but traverses every retained registry entry.
The enumeration assumes each entry still has a backing resource and reads its fields without checking for an inactive entry.
The null dereference, and potentially the mismatch between retained entries and allocated capacity, causes a process-terminating memory-safety failure instead of returning the list

workflow-0150.summary: Inconsistent initial nesting level causes formatting-cache out-of-bounds access
workflow: A low-level structured-data encoder accepts an inconsistent initial nesting level and initializes a formatting cache only for the base level.
Encoding a nested container increases the nesting level and requests cached separator data for a level whose entries do not exist.
The cache-growth helper assumes entries for the previous level and reads beyond the short cache while deriving the next indentation string.
The out-of-bounds read triggers an assertion or heap-buffer-overflow instead of producing a recoverable argument or state error.

workflow-0151.summary: Incompatible module state layout rejected by legacy registration
workflow: A module-like component is created using a managed state layout that is incompatible with legacy global registration.
A caller invokes the legacy registration operation on that component.
The operation detects the incompatible layout and raises an internal system error instead of registering it.

workflow-0153.summary: Reentrant finalization re-registers an object during destruction
workflow: A managed object begins destruction and invokes user-defined finalization logic before teardown is complete.
The finalizer re-registers or otherwise retains the object in a shared registry, changing its lifetime during destruction.
The original teardown continues under the assumption that finalization could not make the object reachable again and releases or invalidates the object’s state.
Later registry use follows the retained entry to storage that teardown has already invalidated, causing a use-after-free or process-terminating failure.

workflow-0156.summary: Teardown ordering preserves callback-retained module allocations
workflow: A module initializer creates a managed type and associated metadata.
A process-wide callback registry retains a callback that keeps the module-created type graph reachable.
Shutdown collects and destroys modules before clearing the callback registry, so the retention cycle remains intact.
Leak detection at process exit reports the type and metadata as indirect leaks instead of clean reclamation.

workflow-0158.summary: Stale optimized execution during runtime finalization triggers an invalid state assertion
workflow: A runtime specializes a frequently executed backward control-flow operation into an optimized form.
Process finalization begins while a suspended computation still retains that specialized operation.
Finalization disables the optimization subsystem without invalidating all already-specialized operations.
Cleanup resumes the suspended computation, which executes the stale optimized operation and invokes optimization logic.
The optimization logic asserts that the subsystem is enabled, detects it is disabled, and aborts instead of safely skipping optimization.

workflow-0162.summary: Zero-length input offset causes boundary-underflow read
workflow: A line-reading routine receives input beginning with an embedded terminator byte, so its string-length calculation reports zero despite additional bytes having been read.
The routine uses the zero length to inspect the preceding buffer element while deciding whether to continue reading.
That index refers before the valid buffer range, causing an out-of-bounds read and undefined behavior.
Without detection, the loop may continue with an unchanged offset, overwrite previously read input on the next read, and process the wrong data instead of safely stopping at the8?

workflow-0163.summary: Unchecked state-field type causes later invalid mapping access
workflow: A state-restoration interface receives a structured record containing several fields, including an optional mapping field.
Validation checks some fields but omits validating the optional mapping field.
A caller supplies a value of the wrong type in that field, so the record is accepted as internal state.
Later execution treats the field as a mapping and performs a lookup through it.
The invalid representation reaches low-level memory access and crashes the process instead of producing a recoverable type error.

workflow-0165.summary: Recovery rewind underestimates decoder output capacity
workflow: A streaming text decoder encounters malformed input and invokes a user-defined recovery handler.
The handler supplies replacement text and rewinds the input position, increasing the amount of input that remains to be processed.
Buffer-capacity accounting underestimates the required space by failing to include the full replacement length together with the newly remaining input.
Decoding reaches an internal capacity invariant with insufficient space and aborts instead of handling the malformed input safely.

workflow-0166.summary: Undersized output buffer causes native write overflow
workflow: A caller supplies an output buffer that is empty or smaller than the native operation’s required result.
The interface forwards the buffer without validating that its capacity is sufficient.
The native operation writes the fixed-size result into the undersized buffer.
The write exceeds the buffer and produces a fatal system error instead of a recoverable argument-size error.

workflow-0168.summary: Worker teardown omits cleanup of private tracing state
workflow: A background worker allocates private tracing state while executing optimized work.
The worker is abandoned when the hosting runtime shuts down, so its per-worker state is cleared through a special teardown path.
That teardown path releases ordinary worker state but omits the tracing allocation.
Leak detection runs after shutdown and reports the unreclaimed tracing state instead of clean termination.

workflow-0169.summary: Instrumented lazy code dispatch dereferences an invalid generated-code address
workflow: A build enables experimental runtime code generation together with undefined-behavior instrumentation.
A bootstrap executable begins ordinary code execution through the runtime’s lazy generated-code dispatch path.
That dispatch path uses an invalid or corrupted generated-code address under the affected toolchain and instrumentation combination.
The trampoline reads through the invalid address, causing an instrumented segmentation fault and aborting the build instead of completing code generation.

workflow-0172.summary: Tracing crosses instrumentation or exception boundaries with stale stack assumptions
workflow: An execution optimizer begins recording a specialized trace for ordinary control flow.
Execution reaches an instrumented operation or exceptional path that invokes monitoring logic.
The optimizer fails to abandon or invalidate the trace before that transfer, allowing tracing to continue across the boundary.
The resulting trace uses stack-state assumptions that no longer match the actual execution path.
Frame cleanup detects the inconsistent residual stack state and aborts instead of safely deoptimizing or completing execution.

workflow-0174.summary: Insufficiently validated structured result causes out-of-bounds read
workflow: A high-level operation delegates part of its computation to an overridable helper that returns a structured result.
The helper returns a result of the expected outer type but with fewer elements than the caller requires.
The caller validates only the outer type and then accesses fixed positions without checking the result length.
The out-of-range access reads beyond the structured result, causing a crash instead of a recoverable validation error.

workflow-0179.summary: Transformed instruction index causes diagnostic table over-read
workflow: A diagnostic formatter receives an optimized instruction whose opcode uses a transformed representation rather than the metadata table’s original index space.
The formatter treats that transformed value as a direct index into a fixed-size global metadata table.
The resulting index points beyond the table’s valid bounds during ordinary diagnostic output.
Memory-safety instrumentation reports a global buffer over-read and terminates the process instead of producing the trace.

workflow-0180.summary: Malformed instruction operand triggers internal assertion
workflow: A caller constructs a low-level instruction record with an operation that does not accept an argument.
The caller supplies a nonzero argument value despite the operation’s operand contract.
The instruction builder validates the record against that contract and triggers an internal assertion.
The process terminates instead of rejecting the malformed instruction through a recoverable argument error.

workflow-0188.summary: Out-of-range empty slice triggers read-position assertion
workflow: A slicing operation computes an empty result because the requested bounds produce no elements, while the derived start position lies outside the data range.
The implementation forwards that out-of-range position to the normal bulk-read path without special-casing the zero-length result.
The bulk-read path asserts that the position is within the backing data even though no bytes need to be read.
The assertion terminates the operation instead of returning an empty result.

workflow-0193.summary: Unchecked numeric-operation result reaches integer-only comparison logic
workflow: A numeric comparison receives an operand whose customizable negation operation returns a value of an incompatible type.
The comparison path assumes the negation result remains an integer and proceeds with integer-specific manipulation.
Low-level comparison logic interprets the incompatible value under the expected numeric representation.
An internal assertion or crash occurs instead of returning a recoverable type error.

workflow-0200.summary: Permitted concurrent release invalidates lock-handoff assertion
workflow: Multiple workers contend for a shared lock, and a waiting worker is granted ownership through a handoff.
The lock semantics allow another worker to release the lock concurrently, potentially clearing its locked state before the handoff recipient finishes returning.
The acquisition routine assumes a successful handoff means the lock must still appear locked and asserts that invariant.
The valid concurrent state triggers an assertion and process termination instead of returning successful acquisition.

workflow-0205.summary: Uninstrumented dependency causes false-positive race reports
workflow: A concurrency test runs with race-detection instrumentation enabled.
The test links against a prebuilt dependency that was compiled without the same instrumentation.
The dependency performs synchronization internally, but those operations are invisible to the instrumented runtime.
Concurrent use of the dependency is therefore reported as a data race even when the dependency’s synchronization is valid.
The instrumented test job fails on the false-positive diagnostic instead of completing successfully.

workflow-0206.summary: Oversized optimized trace corrupts generated-code metadata during cleanup
workflow: A tracing optimizer is configured to accept traces larger than the generated-code subsystem can safely support.
Execution records and compiles an unusually long trace, reaching an internal machine-code size or representation limit.
The resulting executable metadata becomes inconsistent with the generated instruction sequence.
Later cleanup detaches the executable while assuming the metadata still has the expected entry instruction.
The invalid metadata access triggers an assertion or segmentation fault instead of safely rejecting or shortening the trace.

workflow-0207.summary: Overwritten current-state ownership leaks the previous allocation
workflow: An initialization operation allocates resource state and stores it in a single current-state slot.
A later initialization replaces the slot with new state without releasing the previously stored allocation.
The previous allocation loses its only cleanup reference and remains unreachable.
Leak detection reports unreclaimed memory instead of clean reclamation.

workflow-0210.summary: Unchecked missing metadata lookup causes assembler crash
workflow: A low-level instruction is assembled with overlapping or inconsistent variable metadata.
Name resolution returns no valid descriptor for the referenced variable.
The assembler assumes the lookup succeeded and inspects the missing descriptor as a typed object.
The invalid dereference causes a segmentation fault instead of a recoverable metadata error.

workflow-0214.summary: Missing symbolic-value category causes optimizer crash
workflow: An optimizer creates a symbolic value representing the result of a predicate operation.
Its truthiness analysis dispatches on symbolic-value categories but omits the predicate-result category.
The omitted category is processed using an incompatible representation assumption.
Truthiness analysis dereferences invalid state and terminates instead of treating the predicate result as unknown or boolean.

workflow-0215.summary: Retained view writes through released mapped storage
workflow: A persistent file-backed data store keeps its contents directly mapped in memory.
An external actor truncates the backing file while the store remains open.
A later update accesses mapped data assuming the original file layout still exists.
The access reaches invalid backing storage and terminates the process instead of producing a recoverable storage error.

workflow-0216.summary: Malformed executable stream begins with a non-executable placeholder
workflow: A caller manually rewrites an executable instruction stream and inserts a reserved placeholder intended only for embedded metadata at the beginning.
The rewrite shifts the original instructions without updating the stream’s execution boundaries or metadata layout.
The runtime dispatches from the beginning while assuming the stream contains only executable instructions.
Dispatch encounters the reserved placeholder as an instruction, violates an internal execution invariant, and terminates instead of rejecting the malformed stream.

workflow-0221.summary: Instrumented configuration probe hangs during pre-application runtime initialization
workflow: A build configuration enables memory-safety instrumentation and runs a generated probe executable to test a capability.
The instrumented probe enters runtime initialization before its application code begins.
Initialization enters an incompatible startup path and spins indefinitely instead of completing.
The configuration process waits for the probe to finish, so it hangs rather than reporting a probe failure or continuing.

workflow-0223.summary: Failed secondary registration causes double cleanup of an already-owned record
workflow: Initialization allocates a record and successfully registers it under an initial key in a managed table.
Registration under a second key fails after the record is already owned by the table.
Failure cleanup independently releases the record before destroying the table.
Table destruction releases the same record again, causing a double-free and process termination instead of recoverable initialization failure.

workflow-0226.summary: Unchecked boundary state reaches undefined low-level arithmetic or representation access
workflow: A low-level operation receives an extreme, empty, malformed, or otherwise boundary-case input that leaves storage absent, positions out of range, or numeric values outside safe enc
The implementation accepts that state without first validating or normalizing the relevant pointer, range, or representation invariant.
It performs pointer arithmetic, signed shifting, overflow-prone arithmetic, or direct representation access before those preconditions hold; some operations appear to return the-

workflow-0232.summary: Fixed recursion depth no longer reaches the enforced limit
workflow: A deep-recursion test chooses a fixed nesting depth intended to exceed the runtime's recursion threshold.
Build-time instrumentation or hardening changes the effective recursion behavior, so the chosen depth no longer reaches that threshold.
The recursive operation completes without raising the expected recursion-limit error.
The test assertion reports failure even though the runtime remains operational; increasing the tested depth restores the intended boundary condition.

workflow-0233.summary: Concurrent diagnostic traversal dereferences released execution state
workflow: A serializer traverses a shared mutable mapping using non-owning references to its entries.
Another thread removes or replaces an entry, releasing the referenced value while traversal is still in progress.
The serializer attempts to retain or process the invalidated reference after the concurrent mutation.
The stale reference is dereferenced, causing a use-after-free crash instead of a recoverable concurrent-modification error.

workflow-0239.summary: Concurrent collection reaches an object during partially completed destruction
workflow: A managed object reaches destruction with no remaining owners but remains registered with a concurrent cycle-detection collector.
Destruction performs registry removal that can pause other threads before the object is fully torn down.
During that pause, another thread runs collection and reaches the partially deallocated object because it is still registered.
Collection or subsequent cleanup uses the invalid intermediate state, causing a hang or process-terminating memory failure instead of safe destruction.

workflow-0240.summary: Mismatched nested delimiters underflow parser nesting state
workflow: A tokenizer parses nested interpolation expressions containing mismatched delimiters.
When a closing delimiter is encountered, it decrements the current nesting depth without first verifying that a matching opener exists.
The nesting depth becomes negative for the malformed input.
An internal consistency assertion fires instead of returning a recoverable syntax error identifying the unmatched delimiter.

workflow-0241.summary: Concurrent unsynchronized access to shared mutable storage or state
workflow: Multiple threads obtain independent views of the same mutable byte buffer and begin repeated reads and writes concurrently.
One thread writes an element while another reads the same element without synchronization or atomic coordination.
The conflicting accesses form a data race, so observed values and execution behavior are undefined.
Race-detection instrumentation reports the unsynchronized access instead of allowing the workload to complete normally.

workflow-0242.summary: Unsynchronized concurrent access to replaceable, reference-owned object fields
workflow: Multiple threads access a shared object field that points to executable or descriptive state.
One thread replaces the pointed-to value while another thread reads it concurrently.
The read and replacement use ordinary unsynchronized memory access, so the pointer and its ownership transition are observed inconsistently.
Race-detection instrumentation reports a data race instead of allowing concurrent access to complete safely.

workflow-0243.summary: Concurrent evaluation loses shared interrupt state
workflow: Multiple execution contexts concurrently perform evaluations that update shared process-wide state recording an unhandled interrupt.
One context records the interrupt, while another evaluation clears the same shared state as part of its own initialization.
The unsynchronized updates race, allowing the clearing operation to erase the other context’s indication.
A later termination check reads the cleared state and fails to handle the pending interrupt correctly.

workflow-0244.summary: Unsynchronized inspection of concurrently updated synchronization state
workflow: A worker updates shared synchronization-state bits atomically while coordinating with another thread.
A coordinator uses timing-based progress checks and then inspects those shared bits without an atomic or synchronized read.
The inspection can overlap with the worker’s update, creating a data race on the shared state.
Race detection reports the conflicting access and the concurrency test fails instead of completing normally.

workflow-0245.summary: Concurrent handshake cleanup double-frees shared native state
workflow: Two worker threads initiate overlapping secure handshakes through shared native connection state.
One handshake encounters a cleanup path that releases an internal allocation while the other handshake still references or owns it.
The second handshake later performs its own cleanup on the same allocation without coordinated ownership or lifetime protection.
The allocation is released twice, and memory-safety instrumentation aborts the process instead of allowing both handshakes to finish safely.

workflow-0246.summary: Concurrent container mutation races with size inspection
workflow: A shared dynamically sized container is mutated concurrently by one group of workers.
Another group inspects the container’s memory footprint by reading its capacity or backing-storage metadata.
Resizing or removal updates that metadata while the inspection reads it without synchronization.
The conflicting accesses form a data race, producing inconsistent size results or sanitizer-reported failure instead of safe concurrent operation.

workflow-0247.summary: Concurrent reinitialization invalidates a reader's prior bounds check
workflow: Multiple threads concurrently use one shared stateful object, with one thread reinitializing its internal state while another reads from it.
The reader checks an index or boundary condition before the reinitialization changes the related state.
The reader then uses the stale validation result with the newly changed state and accesses beyond the valid state storage.
The invalid read can expose adjacent memory or terminate the process instead of being prevented by synchronized access.

workflow-0248.summary: Concurrent handshakes race on shared connection state
workflow: A concurrency check starts multiple workers performing handshakes through one shared connection configuration.
The connection library maintains mutable configuration state that is not safe for simultaneous handshakes.
Concurrent handshake workers access that shared state without sufficient synchronization.
Race-detection instrumentation reports a data race, causing the check to fail even though the intended configuration-update race is separate.
